did_you_know.text: The term “shittim wood” is usually understood as acacia wood, a tree suited to the desert climate. A cubit was an ancient measure based roughly on the length of a forearm, so its exact length is uncertain.
In the Bible, the word “horn” can also symbolize strength. Elsewhere in the Bible, people are described as grasping the altar’s horns while seeking refuge.

The names of the tools show that each task at the altar had its own instrument: pots, shovels, bowls, forks, and firepans. This shows that service in the Tabernacle required organization and skill, not only sacred objects.

The phrase “hollow with boards” is usually understood as a hollow structure made of panels, though its exact design is not completely clear. This shows that even ancient technical descriptions can leave details open to interpretation.

In the ancient world, the colors blue, purple, and scarlet were made from natural materials and were relatively costly. Using them at the courtyard entrance emphasized the importance and beauty of the place.

The Tabernacle courtyard was rectangular: its length was twice its width, giving it an area of 5,000 square cubits. Since the exact length of a cubit is uncertain, its dimensions cannot be converted into meters with complete precision.

The word “tamid” does not necessarily mean that the lamp burned without interruption every moment; it can describe a regular, ongoing practice. The next verse explains that the lamp was tended from evening until morning as part of a fixed daily routine.
